title: The Case of the Missing Colors
markdown:
Chromaville sat between singing hills, a painter’s dream. Houses blazed like rainbows. Market fruit glowed like jewels. The air hummed with jasmine and warm pastries.

Elowen the hare, quick as lightning, piloted her dandelion-fluff glider and delivered parcels, always wanting a grander sky. Pask, the calm capybara, brewed comforting blends at The Steaming Leaf, lavender and honey, and quietly longed for a ripple in his peaceful days. Niko the gecko painted murals that pulsed with life and wondered what colours lived beyond his painted skies. The town was a bright song.

Then a silent storm swept the valley. When it passed, Chromaville was muted. Colour had flown, leaving a pale whisper.

Elowen’s ears drooped. The glider’s joy went out of it. Mrs Pipkin’s ruby apples turned dusty rose. The sky hung like faded denim. Niko’s painted sunbeam felt weak. The town’s soul seemed drained.

“As if the colour has been borrowed,” Pask murmured, his lavender leaves gone grey.

“Where did it all go?” Niko whispered.

Elowen glided low toward Whispering Canyon, where wildflowers had once been a riot. Grey rock now. Clear jars dotted the stone, each holding a faint smear of missing sunshine.

“Pask. Niko. I found something. Jars. And the missing colours.”

They hurried. The jars were cold. Faint trails led from town.

“As if the wind drank them,” Niko said, pointing to a jar swirling with mist.

Pask offered chamomile from a flask that had, somehow, stayed itself. “Wind spirits are playful. Never thieves. This is different.”

From a crag above, Zephyr the cloud serpent uncoiled. Usually a sunrise of rose and gold, Zephyr was dull grey, tears like colourless rain.

Elowen did not say she had guessed such sadness. She only looked. Zephyr looked lost.

A hiss like dry leaves. The jars rattled. “The wind became lonely,” Zephyr wailed. “It saw your colours, your laughter. It wanted to hold that warmth and did not know how. So it pulled. It trapped the colours. They faded with each stolen breath.”

They saw not a villain. A creature drowning in loneliness. Zephyr’s sadness had painted the storm.

“You were lonely?” Pask asked, stepping forward. “We understand loneliness. Stolen happiness leaves an emptiness, though.”

Niko nodded. “We can bring you friends. Friends who share laughter, not only air.”

Elowen’s spirit rekindled. “Other sprites. Sky creatures to dance with you. We can fill these jars with laughter.”

The canyon changed. Little sprites danced around Zephyr, laughter like bells. Birds sang. Clouds offered playful breezes. Zephyr, given company that was not a theft, felt warmth bloom. With a joyful sigh its wings took back their sunrise. It nudged the jars.

A soft pop. Each jar released trapped wind and stolen pigment. Colour swirled home like a rainbow tide. Elowen, Pask, and Niko watched, hearts up. Sweet scents returned. The ground hummed. The sky bloomed in every shade it had been missing, and a few it seemed to have invented out of relief.

Chromaville shone. Zephyr visited. Wind sprites played tag in the streets. Elowen, Pask, and Niko found their adventure not in a grand quest but in a kindness that gave a lonely weather-creature somewhere to put its heart. The glider, once more, liked the air. Pask’s lavender remembered how to be purple. Niko, on a wall by the canyon road, painted Zephyr in rose and gold, and left a little grey in the corner on purpose, so no one would forget what loneliness had looked like, or how it had been talked out of stealing the town.
characters: Elowen (a hare glider pilot), Pask (a capybara tea maker), Niko (a gecko mural painter)
